test_title: PYST 14: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 11 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Supreme Court's interim order in the Ranveer Allahbadia case (February 2025) is/are correct?

(1). The Supreme Court granted interim protection to Allahbadia but harshly criticised his remarks as obscene and vulgar.

(2). The Court ruled that Allahbadia was free to travel abroad without any restrictions since the remarks were made behind a paywall.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court granted **interim protection** to Ranveer Allahbadia in February 2025, allowing him relief from immediate arrest or legal action.
 
• While granting protection, the Court strongly criticized his remarks, terming them **obscene and vulgar**, emphasizing the need for responsible behavior.
 
• The judgment did not include any ruling allowing unrestricted **foreign travel** for Allahbadia, as the remarks being behind a paywall was not considered a valid justification.
 
• The Court's focus was on balancing freedom of expression with public decency and moral standards.
 
• Option 1 is correct, as only the first statement aligns with the interim order's details.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Interim Protection:**

 
 
• Interim protection is a temporary relief provided by the court to prevent immediate harm or legal consequences while the case is being heard.
 
 
 
• **Freedom of Speech and Expression:**
 
 
• It is a constitutional right under Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution but is subject to reasonable restrictions under Article 19(2).
 
• Restrictions include public morality, decency, and sovereignty of the state.
 
 
 
• **Obscenity in Law:**
 
 
• Obscenity is regulated under Section 292 of the Indian Penal Code, which prohibits the sale, distribution, or exhibition of obscene material.
 
• The judicial interpretation of obscenity often balances moral standards with artistic freedom.
 
 
 
• **Paywalls and Legal Context:**
 
 
• A paywall restricts access to content behind a subscription fee, but it does not exempt creators from legal scrutiny if the content violates laws.
